characterization_methods.key_findings: κ-phase superlattice reflections are weak and diffuse initially and after 2 min, sharper and more intense after 16 min, clearly visible round particles smaller than 5 nm after 4 h, and cuboidal 5–10 nm particles aligned along <100> directions after 64 h.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Austenite diffraction pattern in [001] zone axis (printed panel labels read [100]γ); dark-field images acquired using {100} superlattice reflections.
characterization_methods.purpose: Track the evolution of intragranular κ-phase precipitation during aging at 500 °C.
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) and dark-field imaging

interfaces.interface_notes: κ-phase precipitation is intragranular (inside austenite grains); no explicit interphase coherence is reported.
interfaces.phase_evolution: κ-phase superlattice reflections are weak and diffuse initially and after 2 min; become less diffuse and more intense after 16 min (volume fraction increased); appear as clearly visible round particles smaller than 5 nm after 4 h; and as cuboidal 5–10 nm particles arranged along <100> directions after 64 h.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Parent process (proc_st-1000c-10min-wq); performed before aging at 500 °C.

phases_present.morphology: weak and diffuse superlattice reflections; not resolvable by dark-field imaging
dense speckle of fine bright particles; superlattice spots sharper and more intense
round particles, clearly visible in dark-field imaging, smaller than 5 nm
cuboidal particles arranged in rows along <100> directions of austenite

structures.overall_structure: Austenitic matrix with intragranular κ-phase precipitates; κ-phase reflections are weak and diffuse initially and after 2 min, become sharper and more intense after 16 min (volume fraction increased), appear as round particles smaller than 5 nm after 4 h, and as cuboidal particles between 5 nm and 10 nm arranged along <100> directions of austenite after 64 h.

unmapped_findings: Fig. 8 caption states the austenite diffraction pattern is the [001] zone axis, while the printed panel labels read [100]γ (figure_008).

Even in the initial solution-treated (1000 °C, 10 min) and water-quenched state, diffuse superlattice reflections corresponding to the formation of intragranular κ-phases were already distinguished on the TEM diffraction pattern of austenite (b0046).
The nanosized intragranular κ-phase precipitation inside austenite could lead to important precipitation hardening in this TRIPLEX-grade alloy (b0045).
